questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed in the syllabus coverage for “Managing Multiple Connections”?
questions.explanation: The attached FastAPI syllabus lists “Connection managers” under this lesson. The remaining syllabus subtopics are preserved in the lesson file for complete coverage.

questions.prompt: According to the worked example in “Managing Multiple Connections”, which result should the learner verify?
options: Connect a WebSocket client to /ws and send "hello"; the server replies "echo: hello".
The app publishes itself to production and passes all tests automatically.
HTTP 500 is returned for every valid request.
Input validation and authorization are disabled by design.
questions.answer_key: Connect a WebSocket client to /ws and send "hello"; the server replies "echo: hello".
questions.explanation: The worked example explicitly documents this expected result. Reproduce it locally in the listed environment before treating it as tested behavior.

questions.prompt: Which concurrency/resource decision is most accurate? (Managing Multiple Connections)
options: Use async for non-blocking I/O, bound resources and clean up on cancellation/disconnect
Assume async automatically speeds CPU-heavy computation
Keep every WebSocket open forever after a client disconnects
Use unbounded in-memory task creation for durable jobs
questions.answer_key: Use async for non-blocking I/O, bound resources and clean up on cancellation/disconnect
questions.explanation: Async concerns waiting and lifecycle behavior; CPU-bound work and durable jobs may require separate execution mechanisms.
